nodes.name: Chloride Corrosion of NF
nodes.procedure: Synthesizing multimetallic hydroxide nanosheet arrays supported on NF by fully utilizing high concentration of chloride ions (Cl-) to corrode NF in a one-step route. The NF was corroded to Ni^{2+} ions in a high concentration of Cl- solution occurring in the anode region. Then, the chloride ions continuously migrated and enriched to the anode region. Simultaneously, the oxygen from the air or water reacted with water to form hydroxide (OH-) on the cathode. Finally, the M^{x+} cations and the diffusion of Ni^{2+} synchronously reacted with OH- to precipitate and form multimetallic hydroxide nanosheet arrays supporting on NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: The synthesized monometallic Ni(OH)₂ and bimetallic NiCo-OH hydroxides exhibited no characteristic peak, indicating their amorphous nature. Multimetallic NiCoMo-OH hydroxides exhibited a widely weak peak around 25°, revealing low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline nature of hydroxide nanosheets was analyzed via X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Figure S5). The synthesized monometallic (Ni(OH)₂) and bimetallic (e.g. NiCo-OH) hydroxides exhibited no characteristic peak, indicating their amorphous nature. Additionally, the multimetallic (e.g. NiCoMo-OH) hydroxides exhibited a widely weak peak around 25°, revealing the low crystallinity of these multimetallic hydroxide nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂ peaks at 855.6 eV and 873.2 eV with satellites at 861.6 and 879.6 eV indicate Ni²⁺ oxidation state. Co 2p shows Co²⁺/Co³⁺ with 2p₃/₂ at 781.1 eV and 2p₁/₂ at 796.8 eV (spin-orbit splitting >15 eV). Mo 3d shows Mo⁴⁺ 3d₅/₂ at 231.7 eV and Mo⁶⁺ 3d₃/₂ at 234.9 eV. O 1s at 531 eV for metal-oxygen bonds. Ni5Co3Mo-OH shows Mo 3d and O 1s peaks shifted to lower binding energies vs NiMo-OH, indicating electron transfer.
